title: Weak property rights and lax enforcement fuel tropical forest fires
summary: Indonesian firms burn more forest land when the fire spread risk falls on unclaimed land. Clearer property rights and credible penalties could cut fires by half.

title: How to fund social insurance without pushing workers into informality
summary: Stronger collection of social insurance contributions in China reduced formal firm entry and shifted workers towards informal jobs.

title: Critical minerals scramble: Turning a windfall into development
summary: The global scramble for critical minerals offers resource-rich economies a large but possibly short-lived windfall – one that well-designed contracts, royalties and industrial policy can turn into lasting development rather than another resource curse.

title: Can role models uplift marginalised communities?
summary: In Vietnam, a low-cost video intervention featuring successful entrepreneurs briefly raised ethnic minority farmers' belief in their own agency. However, it did not raise household incomes, and for households hit by natural disasters it may have made things worse.

summary: Rising ocean acidity cuts small-scale fish catches, pushes up seafood prices and worsens women's nutrition, increasing neonatal mortality in coastal communities of low- and middle-income countries by around 5% for each 0.01-unit fall in pH. Cutting emissions, limiting industrial…

title: This week in development economics at VoxDev: 09/10/2026
summary: This week we featured research on interest rates, health insurance, social welfare and more!

title: Mining booms move workers from farms to services, not factories
summary: Global evidence from 2,041 cities linked to 33,262 mines producing 23 minerals shows that resource booms reshape local employment patterns far more than they drive urbanisation.

title: The tradeoffs between sovereign AI and capable AI
summary: Frontier AI capability is only likely to be available to LMICs on conditions priced in sovereignty. How harsh the sovereignty-capability trade-off becomes depends on the fate of open-source AI, which our previous post argued is uncertain, and plausibly deteriorating.

title: How health insurers’ network decisions affect patient mortality
summary: When Colombia shut down its largest health insurer, mortality rose not only among its enrolees but also among patients who were never enrolled with it. The reason is that incumbent insurers reduced the number of hospitals, clinics, and doctors their patients could visit. We show…

title: Paying refugees to go home: Lessons from Afghanistan’s cash-for-return experiment
summary: In 2016, the UN doubled the cash it paid Afghan refugees to leave Pakistan, and 363,000 people went home in the middle of the fighting season. New research finds that policy-induced return reduced insurgent violence but made it deadlier and that it increased social conflict wher…

title: Work over cash: Why employers and workers prefer jobs to handouts
summary: Experiments in Uganda reveal that employers and workers prefer to share income through paid work rather than cash, even when the work produces nothing, suggesting that some overstaffing reflects social support rather than inefficiency.

title: Evidence-based policy: Why one good trial isn't enough
summary: Randomised trials have made development economics more rigorous, yet policymakers still often treat one successful study as proof a programme will work everywhere – a mistake that saw nearly 200 million microcredit loans issued before multiple trials revealed only modest effects…

title: Can Nepal depoliticise its civil service?
summary: Nepal’s civil service serves political parties more than it serves the public, and is a first-order constraint on growth. The new government has a rare opportunity to change this, but it will only work if reformers treat de-politicisation as a political project, not a technical…

title: Does Africa need development economics?
summary: Ken Opalo on the craft of policymaking and the economic research that Africa needs.

title: Asking for help in public: Why eligible people may not claim welfare
summary: A lab experiment in Côte d’Ivoire finds that making applications for cash support public reduced unsuccessful claims but also deterred more than one in four eligible participants.

title: When central banks change interest rates, do borrowers feel it?
summary: Interest rates paid by households and firms move much less with monetary policy rates in poorer countries than in richer ones, and for households in the poorest countries, they tend to move in the opposite direction.
